sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: Which component of physical fitness refers to the ability of our muscles to perform exercises continuously over a prolonged duration?
questions.answer: A) Muscular Endurance

questions.question_text: What does BMI stand for in the context of health metrics?
questions.answer: B) Body Mass Index

questions.question_text: Which ability is crucial for quickly changing body direction without losing balance?
questions.answer: B) Agility

questions.question_text: In a 100-meter sprint, which phase follows the starting block push-off?
questions.answer: B) Acceleration phase

questions.question_text: True or False: Warming up before vigorous physical activity decreases the risk of muscle injuries.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question_text: Which of these is a track-and-field throwing event?
questions.answer: B) Shot Put

questions.question_text: Cardiovascular endurance relates primarily to the efficiency of which two organs?
questions.answer: B) Heart and Lungs

questions.question_text: True or False: Good posture only affects appearance and has no impact on physical well-being.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: Which of the following activities best improves joint flexibility?
questions.answer: C) Static Stretching

questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of the 'Baton' in athletics?
options: B) To be passed between runners in a relay race
D) To signal the start of a race
questions.answer: B) To be passed between runners in a relay race

questions.question_text: Define the term 'Motor Fitness' and name one fitness drill used to measure it in school. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Motor fitness is the ability of an individual to perform physical movements efficiently. It includes traits like balance and agility, which can be measured using a shuttle run test.

questions.question_text: Why is personal hygiene considered a vital part of individual well-being? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Personal hygiene prevents the spread of diseases and infections. Maintaining cleanliness keeps the body healthy, boosting confidence and contributing to overall physical well-being.

questions.question_text: State the difference between 'Health-related' and 'Skill-related' physical fitness components. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Health-related fitness focuses on overall body wellness and preventing disease (e.g., endurance). Skill-related fitness focuses on abilities needed for sports performance, such as speed and coordination.

questions.question_text: Name the four distinct phases of a long jump in athletics. [15-25 words]
questions.answer: The four distinct phases of a long jump are the approach run, takeoff, flight through the air, and landing.

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the role of a 'cool down' routine after intense exercise. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: A cool down slowly lowers the heart rate and relaxes muscles. It prevents sudden dizziness and helps reduce muscle soreness after intense physical exertion.

questions.question_text: Describe the proper mechanical posture and starting position a runner must maintain during a short-distance sprint start. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The runner must place their feet securely in the starting blocks and bend down with hands spaced shoulder-width apart behind the line. At the 'set' cue, they raise their hips higher than their shoulders, keeping their eyes focused on the track ahead.

questions.question_text: Explain how participating regularly in physical education classes improves a student's cardiovascular endurance over time. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Regular participation involves continuous aerobic exercises like running or swimming. Over time, this forces the heart muscle to grow stronger and pump blood more efficiently, while the lungs expand their capacity to deliver oxygen, thereby improving overall cardiovascular endurance.

questions.question_text: List the sequence of actions required to perform a proper underhand relay baton pass between two athletes. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The incoming runner carries the baton in one hand. As they approach, the outgoing runner extends their opposite hand backward, palm facing up. The incoming runner places the baton smoothly into the open hand with an upward sweeping motion.

questions.question_text: Define 'Coordination' as a motor fitness skill and give an example of an athletic activity that heavily relies on it. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Coordination is the ability to use different body parts together smoothly and efficiently. An athletic activity that relies heavily on coordination is hurdling, where the runner must synchronize sprinting speed with precise leg lifting and arm balance to clear obstacles.

questions.question_text: Ravi has been skipping his physical education classes and spends most of his time sitting. Recently, he complains of poor stamina and back pain. Discuss how the lack of physical activity affects his health metrics and suggest two fundamental athletic drills to help him recover his fitness. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Skipping physical activity causes muscle weakness, leading to back pain, and reduces cardiovascular efficiency, lowering his stamina. His BMI might also rise due to inactivity. To recover, Ravi should begin with light jogging to rebuild his aerobic endurance and practice dynamic stretching drills, like lunges, to restore his flexibility and core strength.

questions.question_text: During track-and-field practice, a student struggles to throw the shot put effectively because they rely only on arm strength. Detail the correct mechanical technique for a shot put throw, emphasizing the sequence of muscle engagement from the lower body to the release. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Effective shot put relies on the entire body. The student must start in a crouched stance, using strong leg muscles to drive forcefully across the throwing circle. As they rotate forward, the momentum transfers from the hips to the torso, and finally through the shoulder and arm, releasing the shot put powerfully with a snapping wrist motion.
